description: Two silent-unless-relevant hook sets. The dashboard-kit notice: one line at session start or /clear in a repository that owns a Fabric service whose dashboard has no kit or an older one (fabric-dashboard/0.1, DEC-0036), phrased as an upgrade the agent may make itself. The Fabric session hooks (working-with-fabric, COM-04, FAA-12a): at session start or /clear, the preamble when Claude Code has the MCP server `fabric` and Fabric runs (fabric_whoami, then the project board through com.status and com.list, claim and release); when Fabric is down, one line, only in a project that uses Fabric (a Fabric contract file, a project-bound registration or a service descriptor naming the repository); nothing on compact or resume; each turn's facts (HEAD, files changed, lines added and removed, never content), the board's unread count, and, once the running Fabric's fabric_session_observe takes them (unless FABRIC_SESSION_NO_REPOSITORIES=1), the other repositories the turn touched (the last 512 KB of the session transcript, message text and tool output included (a secret the session displayed can be there; read in memory only), is then read and only the current turn's tool names and path arguments are used; host/owner/name leave the machine, never a local path or text) and the session's end through Fabric, only when the running Fabric advertises session-hooks/1; at each prompt one line only when the unread count rose, then each nudge a turn's answer carried, once (watch-mail prints those of turns it delivered). All silent in a session Fabric launched but the exit contract and the prompt hook's verdict on it and the retro line below. Every hook reads no Fabric token (a credential embedded in an origin URL is read by git config and dropped in memory, never spooled or sent), prints at most one block, always exits 0 once python3 starts (on Windows it must name Python in Git Bash, FAA-183), and hands any Fabric call to a detached worker with a 10 s deadline. In a session Fabric started on a board request (FABRIC_DISPATCH_WORKFLOW), session start prints the exit contract instead of the preamble on the condition that the session's own prompt starts with the dispatch line naming the same three, launched or not, and the prompt hook, which sees that line, confirms the run or says it is none, launched or not, with no unread line or nudge, and the dashboard-kit notice says nothing (FAA-201). After a call to Fabric's fabric_work_release or fabric_task_release that releases a claim as done, PostToolUse adds one line naming the retro (FAA-206); after any other call, or a release Fabric's answer refuses (released: false, already-released) or that released nothing, nothing.
